welcome_message: Create a Skyulf training project. Choose single_model for one model, model_competition for 2-8 candidates sharing one target, or multi_target for 2-8 independent target branches. Select local or Spark inference based on expected rows and bytes per scoring run and available compute. Spark inference trains with pandas and requires partition-safe steps. Select models, ensemble members and training settings in setup; editable model-owned settings and Core-derived search spaces are generated automatically. Model and combined business rules live in src/features/scoring.py. Initialization creates local files only.

training_layout.description: Training layout: single_model = guided model setup; multi_target = shared setup, then define target/model recipes in config/training.yml and score them as one versioned model set; model_competition = compare candidates for one target using shared CV, then select one winner; select models below and generate editable config/training.yml

project_name.description: 1. Data | Project folder and Bundle name (letters, digits and underscores)

inference_mode.description: 1. Data | Inference per run: local loads predictions within local row/byte limits; spark distributes MLflow pyfunc scoring. Estimate expected rows and bytes per inference run and available worker memory. Spark uses pandas training and admits only partition-safe preprocessing; unsupported steps fail before scoring.

engine.description: 1. Data | Local training and inference library: pandas or Polars; Spark inference always trains with pandas

task.description: 1. Data | What will the model predict? regression = a number; classification = a category

catalog.description: Optional init-file test catalog; otherwise configure deployment/variables.yml

schema.description: Optional init-file test schema; otherwise configure deployment/variables.yml

source_table_name.description: 1. Data | Training INPUT table: existing rows with features and known answers. Enter table name only; blank uses <project_name>_source

score_source_table_name.description: 1. Data | Prediction INPUT table: rows the model will read to make predictions. This is NOT the output table. Blank = same input as training

prediction_table_name.description: 1. Data | Prediction OUTPUT table name, e.g. customer_predictions. Results are written here; blank uses <project_name>_predictions

record_key_columns.description: 1. Data | Columns identifying one record, e.g. customer_id or customer_id, observation_id. Separate names with commas; no brackets or quotes

input_columns.description: 1. Data | Columns the model learns from, e.g. income, age, balance. Separate names with commas; exclude record keys and the answer column

target_column.description: 1. Data | Column containing the known answer during training, e.g. churn or claim_amount

training_version.description: 1. Data | Training table snapshot number from Databricks table History, e.g. 0 or 12 (not a model version). null = resolve latest once at run start; an explicit version pins that snapshot for manual and scheduled runs

cv_enabled.description: 1. Cross-validation | Use several training-only folds to score search candidates? No duplicate post-search CV report. With CV off, search uses a training-only validation split. Final test rows stay separate. Defaults: 5-fold K-fold, shuffle enabled, seed 42; the following questions select the fold policy before the data window. Model competition always enables the shared CV policy.

cv_folds.description: 1. Cross-validation | How many CV splits? 5 means five evaluations; more splits take longer (2-20)

cv_type.description: 1. Cross-validation | Fold method: k_fold, stratified_k_fold, time_series_split, shuffle_split, group_k_fold, stratified_group_k_fold, or nested_cv. Nested CV repeats an independent inner search in every outer training fold, then runs a separate final search Temporal CV automatically selects a chronological final holdout; its clock/window questions follow.

cv_inner_folds.description: 1. Cross-validation | Inner search folds for nested CV (2-20). Leave blank for the Core default. The strategy budget applies to every outer-fold search and the final search.

cv_nested_type.description: 1. Cross-validation | Policy at both nested levels; auto selects stratified classification or regression K-fold. Temporal requires a temporal final holdout and event_column.

cv_group_column.description: 1. Cross-validation | Group identity column, excluded from features. Final holdout isolates whole groups; disable holdout stratify.

cv_gap.description: 1. Cross-validation | Rows excluded before each temporal validation window at both nested levels.

cv_test_size.description: 1. Cross-validation | Temporal validation rows per fold; null uses the Core default.

cv_max_train_size.description: 1. Cross-validation | Temporal training rows; null expands, an integer creates a rolling window.

cv_shuffle.description: 1. Cross-validation | Shuffle rows for CV? Use false for time_series_split, true for shuffle_split

cv_random_state.description: 1. Cross-validation | Seed for repeatable CV splits. Keep 42 unless you want different splits

split_strategy.description: 1. Data | How to reserve test rows? random = random rows; temporal = newer rows for testing and older rows for training. Default source: full snapshot for random, rolling calendar for temporal. Override training_window_mode in an init file.

test_size.description: 1. Data | Share of rows reserved for final testing: 0.2 means 20% test and 80% training

random_state.description: 1. Data | Seed for repeatable random splitting. Keep 42 unless you want a different split

stratify.description: 1. Data | Keep similar proportions of each target class in training and test rows?

training_window_mode.description: 1. Data | Which source rows to use? full_snapshot = all; fixed_window = dates you enter; rolling_calendar = recent complete months; rolling_days = last N elapsed UTC days; auto = all for random, recent months for temporal

window_timezone.description: 1. Data | Timezone defining calendar month boundaries, e.g. Europe/Copenhagen. This controls selected data, not when the job runs

monthly_lookback_months.description: 1. Data | Total complete past months to read, including the final holdout. Example: 4 months with a 2-month holdout leaves 2 months for training

holdout_months.description: 1. Data | How many final complete months to hold out for testing? Enter 1 to total lookback minus 1; example: 2

event_column.description: 1. Data | Column containing when each record was observed, e.g. observation_date; used to select older/newer data

event_time_kind.description: 1. Data | How is this column stored? timestamp = database timestamp representing an instant; local_timestamp = database date/time without timezone; date = day only; text = a string. Choose yourself; setup does not inspect the table

event_text_kind.description: 1. Data | What does the date text contain? offset_datetime = date/time with Z or +02:00; local_datetime = date/time without an offset; date = only a day, e.g. 2026-08-10

event_time_timezone.description: 1. Data | Which location does this clock/date belong to? Enter e.g. Europe/Copenhagen or UTC

event_date_only.description: 1. Data | This column has a day but no time. May we treat it as the start of that day? midnight = yes, 00:00 in your chosen timezone; reject = stop if such a value is encountered

start.description: 1. Data | Earliest observation to include, e.g. 2026-06-01T00:00:00+02:00. Required for fixed_window; rolling_calendar calculates it for every run

holdout_start.description: 1. Data | Observations from this time onward are test rows, e.g. 2026-08-01T00:00:00+02:00. Older selected rows train the model; rolling runs calculate it

cutoff.description: 1. Data | Stop before this observation time, e.g. 2026-09-01T00:00:00+02:00. This is a data boundary, not the job date; rolling runs calculate it

filter_unavailable_results.description: 1. Data | Do answers become known later? true = exclude rows whose answer was not yet available at the chosen time; false = use supplied answers

result_availability_lag_hours.description: 1. Data | When result_cutoff is blank, subtract this many hours from run start. Enter 0 to 87600; example: 48 excludes results available in the last two days. An explicit result_cutoff overrides this lag for every run

result_available_at_column.description: 1. Data | Column recording when each answer became known, e.g. claim_confirmed_at. This is a column name, not a date you enter

result_time_kind.description: 1. Data | How is this column stored? timestamp = database timestamp representing an instant; local_timestamp = database date/time without timezone; date = day only; text = a string. Choose yourself; setup does not inspect the table

result_text_kind.description: 1. Data | What does the date text contain? offset_datetime = date/time with Z or +02:00; local_datetime = date/time without an offset; date = only a day, e.g. 2026-08-10

result_time_timezone.description: 1. Data | Which location does this clock/date belong to? Enter e.g. Europe/Copenhagen or UTC

result_date_only.description: 1. Data | This column has a day but no time. May we treat it as the start of that day? midnight = yes, 00:00 in your chosen timezone; reject = stop if such a value is encountered

result_cutoff.description: 1. Data | Use answers known by this time, INCLUDING this instant, e.g. 2026-09-15T00:00:00+02:00. An explicit cutoff applies to every run; blank derives run start minus result_availability_lag_hours

max_rows.description: 1. Data | Maximum rows transferred into Python memory per read; exceeding this stops the run. This does not randomly sample rows

max_input_mb.description: 1. Data | Maximum input data size transferred into Python memory, in MiB (64 = 64 MiB). Model training can use more RAM

training_sample_rows.description: 1. Data | Optional sample: enter 10000 to select up to 10000 eligible rows BEFORE train/test splitting. null = no sampling. Prediction rows are never sampled

training_sample_seed.description: 1. Data | Seed for choosing the same sample from the same table snapshot. Keep 42 unless you want another sample

sample_weight_enabled.description: Use sample weights? false = No (default); true = Yes.

weight_column.description: Training-only sample-weight column (excluded from model features).

model_params.description: Optional init-file fixed model params. For custom fixed params, Core resolves the automatic search space; otherwise generated model settings include editable search lists.

search_strategy.description: 3. Validation and search | Choose grid, random, halving_grid, halving_random, or optional Optuna. Core supplies a model-appropriate default search space; grid strategies evaluate its full Cartesian product

search_settings.description: 3. Validation and search | Use Core defaults for this strategy, or customize its controls below

search_max_candidates.description: 3. Validation and search | Maximum full-grid combinations to admit (1-10000). Grid and halving_grid run every combination, so preflight rejects a larger space

search_space.description: 3. Validation and search | Optional init-file override: JSON object mapping model parameters to finite candidate lists. {} uses the selected model's Core default search space

regression_search_metric.description: 3. Validation and search | Objective for choosing regression parameters on training folds; separate from the heldout lifecycle metric

classification_search_metric.description: 3. Validation and search | Objective for choosing classification parameters on training folds; separate from the heldout lifecycle metric

search_n_trials.description: 3. Validation and search | Trials or initial sampled candidates for random, halving_random and Optuna (1-1000)

search_timeout.description: 3. Validation and search | Optional Optuna soft stop in positive seconds; null disables it. A running estimator fit is not interrupted

search_random_state.description: 3. Validation and search | Seed for sampled parameter choices, separate from the heldout split seed and CV fold seed

search_factor.description: 3. Validation and search | Successive halving keeps roughly one in this many candidates per round (integer 2 or more)

search_resource.description: 3. Validation and search | Halving budget resource: training rows or estimator n_estimators. n_estimators requires explicit max_resources and a compatible model

search_min_resources.description: 3. Validation and search | Halving starting budget: exhaust, smallest, or a positive integer

search_estimator_min_resources.description: 3. Validation and search | Starting estimator budget for n_estimators halving (integer 2 or more; must not exceed max_resources)

search_max_resources.description: 3. Validation and search | Maximum estimator resource count for n_estimators halving; enter a positive integer compatible with the selected model

search_sampler.description: 3. Validation and search | Optuna sampler: TPE, random or CMA-ES; CMA-ES samples categorical axes randomly

search_pruner.description: 3. Validation and search | Optuna trial pruner; Core checks whether the selected model and validation method support early stopping. none disables pruning

search_pruning.description: 3. Validation and search | Allow Optuna pruning when model and validation settings support it

search_tune_threshold.description: 3. Cross-validation | Select a binary decision threshold from inner out-of-fold predictions. Requires probability output; final holdout stays untouched.

retraining_mode.description: 4. Lifecycle | Start training yourself, or enable automatic training on your cron schedule after deployment

retraining_cron_expression.description: 4. Lifecycle | When to train (Quartz cron)? 0 0 3 3 * ? = monthly on day 3 at 03:00; 0 0 3 1 1,7 ? = Jan 1 and Jul 1 at 03:00. Does not set the data window

retraining_timezone_id.description: 4. Lifecycle | Timezone for the job clock: Europe/Copenhagen means 03:00 Copenhagen time. UTC means 03:00 UTC. This does not change dates in your data

retraining_pause_status.description: 4. Lifecycle | Enable the training clock after deployment (UNPAUSED), or keep it paused (PAUSED)?

scoring_mode.description: 4. Lifecycle | Start scoring yourself, or schedule it independently of training?

scoring_cron_expression.description: 4. Lifecycle | When to score (Quartz cron)? 0 0 * * * ? runs hourly. This does not change the training window

scoring_timezone_id.description: 4. Lifecycle | Timezone for the scoring clock, e.g. UTC or Europe/Copenhagen. Independent of the training clock and source dates

scoring_pause_status.description: 4. Lifecycle | Enable the scoring clock after deployment (UNPAUSED), or keep it paused (PAUSED)?

model_change_mode.description: 4. Lifecycle | When the selected model/model set changes: incremental_append keeps old predictions and scores new rows; full_rebuild recomputes the complete source with the new selection. Independent of source UPDATE/DELETE handling

auto_rebuild_on_cdf_expiry.description: 4. Lifecycle | Automatically rebuild predictions when retained Delta change history has expired? Adds a visible recovery task to the score job. May rescore the full source; independent of model-change policy

score_model_selection.description: 4. Lifecycle | Score with one pinned version or resolve the controlled champion on each run

promotion_policy.description: 4. Lifecycle | Require operator approval or promote automatically after quality gates pass

score_handoff.description: 4. Lifecycle | Optionally start the score job after successful champion initialization, promotion or rollback (single, competition or model set). Pending approval, failed quality and rejection do not start scoring

regression_metric.description: 4. Lifecycle | Metric for comparing regression models on separate test data (heldout). Lower error is better; higher R2 or explained variance is better

classification_metric.description: 4. Lifecycle | Metric for comparing classification models on separate test data (heldout). Some metrics need probabilities or specific class counts

min_improvement.description: 4. Lifecycle | Minimum metric improvement required for manual or automatic promotion; ties never pass

quality_threshold.description: 4. Lifecycle | Absolute quality gate; numeric required for automatic promotion or manual first-champion approval. Choose for your metric and task.

risk_category.description: 4. Lifecycle | Optional business risk label (e.g. Low, Medium, High); leave blank when unused. This label does not change promotion gates.

compute_mode.description: 5. Compute | Job compute mode for this project

spark_version.description: 5. Compute | Approved Databricks ML Runtime for the job cluster

cost_tag_key.description: 5. Compute | Approved cluster cost tag key, for example CostCenter or PayingRegNo

cost_tag_value.description: 5. Compute | Approved cluster cost tag value; for PayingRegNo, enter your paying registration number

model_set_name.description: 6. Multi-model outputs | Registered MODEL SET name (not a table). Blank = <project_name>_set; enter your own name to override. Target catalog/metadata schema and dev suffix are added automatically

model_set_output_mode.description: 6. Multi-model outputs | all = save every model prediction and business result together; combined_only = run the models but save only combined business results plus keys/status/version (requires rules); separate_views = save all results once and expose model/business columns through separately named views, without duplicate tables

model_set_table_name.description: 6. Multi-model outputs | Physical result table name. Blank = <project_name>_set_scores. Target catalog/schema and dev suffix are added automatically

model_view_prefix.description: 6. Multi-model outputs | Prefix for each model view: <prefix>_<branch>. Blank = <project_name>_predictions. Customize individual names or select models in config/inference.yml (model_set)

combined_view_name.description: 6. Multi-model outputs | Combined business result view name. Blank = <project_name>_business_results. Created only when the saved set has combined rules

source_change_policy.description: 6. Multi-model outputs | If existing source rows are updated/deleted: reject = stop and keep previous results; rebuild_on_change = rescore the full current snapshot with the selected model set, rebuilding lag/rolling history. New inserts still append. Full data must fit row/byte limits. Independent of the model-change setting

model_set_promotion_policy.description: 6. Model set lifecycle | manual_approval = review then approve; automatic = activate the complete set only when EVERY branch passes its saved quality_threshold, additional quality_gates and improvement over its counterpart in the current champion set. Configure metrics in multi_model.py. First sets require absolute thresholds. Score runs separately

personal_development_targets.description: 6. Deployment | Add personal development targets inside test, syst and prod workspaces? Jobs and outputs stay user-scoped; schedules start paused

deployment_identity.description: 6. Deployment | Shared targets: keep existing deployment ownership, use one service principal, or separate train/score principals; configure IDs in deployment/variables.yml

manage_job_permissions.description: 6. Deployment | Manage shared job permissions in this Bundle? false = keep access managed by your existing platform; true = configure deployment/variables.yml

evaluation_charts_enabled.description: Evaluation charts | Add a separate generate_charts task and MLflow Image grid diagnostics? Saves up to 2000 heldout prediction/label rows per evaluated model in MLflow. Includes regression/classification diagnostics, supported model importance, competition comparison or independent model-set reports. Adds Matplotlib; no extra training.

shap_enabled.description: Model explanations | Generate optional SHAP importance and sample waterfall charts using training rows only? Applies to single models, competition candidates and all generated branches; adds training runtime dependencies

shap_max_samples.description: Model explanations | Maximum training rows to explain (1-200). Smaller budgets reduce SHAP computation, especially for ensembles

shap_max_features.description: Model explanations | Maximum transformed features (1-50). This is a guard, NOT top-K selection: exceeding it reports unavailable without computing SHAP

shap_max_display_samples.description: Model explanations | Number of sample waterfalls to save/show (0-50; cannot exceed explained rows). 0 keeps only global importance; enter e.g. 3 for individual explanations

include_daily_rollout.description: Online serving | Add a paused daily traffic rollout job? Uses an explicitly initialized rollout, verified monitoring, 10 percentage-point stages lasting at least 24 hours, and guarded champion promotion after the final stage passes. Configure config/serving.yml before enabling.

include_online_publication.description: Online features | Add a paused hourly publication job? Triggers native synchronization from one explicitly selected latest-value Delta feature table into an existing online store. Configure config/serving.yml before enabling.

lookback_days.description: 1. Data | Total elapsed 24-hour days before each run to read, including holdout; enter 1 to 36500

holdout_days.description: 1. Data | Final elapsed days reserved for temporal testing; enter 1 to lookback_days minus 1

branch_count.description: Model set | How many independent targets should be trained? Configure each branch below; Bundle generates editable multi_model.py.

branch_1_name.description: Branch 1 | Unique branch name (portable identifier); also names its registered model

branch_1_task.description: Branch 1 | What will the model predict? regression = a number; classification = a category

branch_1_sample_weight_enabled.description: Use sample weights? false = No (default); true = Yes.

branch_1_weight_column.description: Training-only sample-weight column (excluded from model features).

branch_1_target_column.description: Branch 1 | Column containing the known answer during training, e.g. churn or claim_amount

branch_1_input_columns.description: Branch 1 | Columns the model learns from, e.g. income, age, balance. Separate names with commas; exclude record keys and the answer column

branch_1_preprocessing_recipe.description: Branch 1 | Named recipe from config/preprocessing.yml: default, none, example_imputer, example_frequency, example_imputer_frequency or example_all; adapt recipe columns to this branch

branch_1_pre_split_recipe.description: Branch 1 | Named recipe from config/pre_split.yml: default, none, example_complete_inputs or example_all; adapt recipe columns to this branch

branch_1_cv_enabled.description: Branch 1 | Use several training-only folds to score search candidates? No duplicate post-search CV report. With CV off, search uses a training-only validation split. Final test rows stay separate. Defaults: 5-fold K-fold, shuffle enabled, seed 42; the following questions select the fold policy before the data window. Model competition always enables the shared CV policy.

branch_1_cv_folds.description: Branch 1 | How many CV splits? 5 means five evaluations; more splits take longer (2-20)

branch_1_cv_type.description: Branch 1 | Fold method: k_fold, stratified_k_fold, time_series_split, shuffle_split, group_k_fold, stratified_group_k_fold, or nested_cv. Nested CV repeats an independent inner search in every outer training fold, then runs a separate final search Temporal CV automatically selects a chronological final holdout; its clock/window questions follow.

branch_1_cv_inner_folds.description: Branch 1 | Inner search folds for nested CV (2-20). Leave blank for the Core default. The strategy budget applies to every outer-fold search and the final search.

branch_1_cv_nested_type.description: Branch 1 | Policy at both nested levels; auto selects stratified classification or regression K-fold. Temporal requires a temporal final holdout and event_column.

branch_1_cv_group_column.description: Branch 1 | Group identity column, excluded from features. Final holdout isolates whole groups; disable holdout stratify.

branch_1_cv_gap.description: Branch 1 | Rows excluded before each temporal validation window at both nested levels.

branch_1_cv_test_size.description: Branch 1 | Temporal validation rows per fold; null uses the Core default.

branch_1_cv_max_train_size.description: Branch 1 | Temporal training rows; null expands, an integer creates a rolling window.

branch_1_cv_shuffle.description: Branch 1 | Shuffle rows for CV? Use false for time_series_split, true for shuffle_split

branch_1_cv_random_state.description: Branch 1 | Seed for repeatable CV splits. Keep 42 unless you want different splits

branch_1_split_strategy.description: Branch 1 | How to reserve test rows? random = random rows; temporal = newer rows for testing and older rows for training. Default source: full snapshot for random, rolling calendar for temporal. Override training_window_mode in an init file.

branch_1_test_size.description: Branch 1 | Share of rows reserved for final testing: 0.2 means 20% test and 80% training

branch_1_random_state.description: Branch 1 | Seed for repeatable random splitting. Keep 42 unless you want a different split

branch_1_stratify.description: Branch 1 | Keep similar proportions of each target class in training and test rows?

branch_1_training_window_mode.description: Branch 1 | Which source rows to use? full_snapshot = all; fixed_window = dates you enter; rolling_calendar = recent complete months; rolling_days = last N elapsed UTC days; auto = all for random, recent months for temporal

branch_1_lookback_days.description: Branch 1 | Total elapsed 24-hour days before each run to read, including holdout; enter 1 to 36500

branch_1_holdout_days.description: Branch 1 | Final elapsed days reserved for temporal testing; enter 1 to lookback_days minus 1

branch_1_window_timezone.description: Branch 1 | Timezone defining calendar month boundaries, e.g. Europe/Copenhagen. This controls selected data, not when the job runs

branch_1_monthly_lookback_months.description: Branch 1 | Total complete past months to read, including the final holdout. Example: 4 months with a 2-month holdout leaves 2 months for training

branch_1_holdout_months.description: Branch 1 | How many final complete months to hold out for testing? Enter 1 to total lookback minus 1; example: 2

branch_1_event_column.description: Branch 1 | Column containing when each record was observed, e.g. observation_date; used to select older/newer data

branch_1_event_time_kind.description: Branch 1 | How is this column stored? timestamp = database timestamp representing an instant; local_timestamp = database date/time without timezone; date = day only; text = a string. Choose yourself; setup does not inspect the table

branch_1_event_text_kind.description: Branch 1 | What does the date text contain? offset_datetime = date/time with Z or +02:00; local_datetime = date/time without an offset; date = only a day, e.g. 2026-08-10

branch_1_event_time_format.description: Branch 1 | How should this date text be read? Example: 10/08/2026 14:30 -> %d/%m/%Y %H:%M; 2026-08-10 -> %Y-%m-%d; 2026-08-10T14:30:00+02:00 -> %Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z

branch_1_event_time_timezone.description: Branch 1 | Which location does this clock/date belong to? Enter e.g. Europe/Copenhagen or UTC

branch_1_event_date_only.description: Branch 1 | This column has a day but no time. May we treat it as the start of that day? midnight = yes, 00:00 in your chosen timezone; reject = stop if such a value is encountered

branch_1_start.description: Branch 1 | Earliest observation to include, e.g. 2026-06-01T00:00:00+02:00. Required for fixed_window; rolling_calendar calculates it for every run

branch_1_holdout_start.description: Branch 1 | Observations from this time onward are test rows, e.g. 2026-08-01T00:00:00+02:00. Older selected rows train the model; rolling runs calculate it

branch_1_cutoff.description: Branch 1 | Stop before this observation time, e.g. 2026-09-01T00:00:00+02:00. This is a data boundary, not the job date; rolling runs calculate it

branch_1_filter_unavailable_results.description: Branch 1 | Do answers become known later? true = exclude rows whose answer was not yet available at the chosen time; false = use supplied answers

branch_1_result_availability_lag_hours.description: Branch 1 | When result_cutoff is blank, subtract this many hours from run start. Enter 0 to 87600; example: 48 excludes results available in the last two days. An explicit result_cutoff overrides this lag for every run

branch_1_result_available_at_column.description: Branch 1 | Column recording when each answer became known, e.g. claim_confirmed_at. This is a column name, not a date you enter

branch_1_result_time_kind.description: Branch 1 | How is this column stored? timestamp = database timestamp representing an instant; local_timestamp = database date/time without timezone; date = day only; text = a string. Choose yourself; setup does not inspect the table

branch_1_result_text_kind.description: Branch 1 | What does the date text contain? offset_datetime = date/time with Z or +02:00; local_datetime = date/time without an offset; date = only a day, e.g. 2026-08-10

branch_1_result_time_format.description: Branch 1 | How should this date text be read? Example: 10/08/2026 14:30 -> %d/%m/%Y %H:%M; 2026-08-10 -> %Y-%m-%d; 2026-08-10T14:30:00+02:00 -> %Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z

branch_1_result_time_timezone.description: Branch 1 | Which location does this clock/date belong to? Enter e.g. Europe/Copenhagen or UTC

branch_1_result_date_only.description: Branch 1 | This column has a day but no time. May we treat it as the start of that day? midnight = yes, 00:00 in your chosen timezone; reject = stop if such a value is encountered

branch_1_result_cutoff.description: Branch 1 | Use answers known by this time, INCLUDING this instant, e.g. 2026-09-15T00:00:00+02:00. An explicit cutoff applies to every run; blank derives run start minus result_availability_lag_hours

branch_1_max_rows.description: Branch 1 | Maximum rows transferred into Python memory per read; exceeding this stops the run. This does not randomly sample rows

branch_1_max_input_mb.description: Branch 1 | Maximum input data size transferred into Python memory, in MiB (64 = 64 MiB). Model training can use more RAM

branch_1_training_sample_rows.description: Branch 1 | Optional sample: enter 10000 to select up to 10000 eligible rows BEFORE train/test splitting. null = no sampling. Prediction rows are never sampled

branch_1_training_sample_seed.description: Branch 1 | Seed for choosing the same sample from the same table snapshot. Keep 42 unless you want another sample

branch_1_regression_model.description: Branch 1 | Choose a regression model. It starts with its default settings; README explains how to change them

branch_1_regression_model_weighted.description: Branch 1 | Choose a regression model. It starts with its default settings; README explains how to change them

branch_1_classification_model.description: Branch 1 | Choose a classification model. It starts with its default settings; README explains how to change them

branch_1_classification_model_weighted.description: Branch 1 | Choose a classification model. It starts with its default settings; README explains how to change them

branch_1_model_params.description: Branch 1 | Optional JSON object of fixed model parameters. For voting/stacking, include base_estimators and any base_estimator_params or final_estimator to define the ensemble. Other models can set this in an init file or generated config

branch_1_search_strategy.description: Branch 1 | Choose grid, random, halving_grid, halving_random, or optional Optuna. Core supplies a model-appropriate default search space; grid strategies evaluate its full Cartesian product

branch_1_search_settings.description: Branch 1 | Use Core defaults for this strategy, or customize its controls below

branch_1_search_max_candidates.description: Branch 1 | Maximum full-grid combinations to admit (1-10000). Grid and halving_grid run every combination, so preflight rejects a larger space

branch_1_search_space.description: Optional init-file search override; otherwise Bundle writes Core-derived editable lists into this branch. Edit its generated search_space or clear it to {} for automatic resolution.

branch_1_regression_search_metric.description: Branch 1 | Objective for choosing regression parameters on training folds; separate from the heldout lifecycle metric

branch_1_classification_search_metric.description: Branch 1 | Objective for choosing classification parameters on training folds; separate from the heldout lifecycle metric

branch_1_search_n_trials.description: Branch 1 | Trials or initial sampled candidates for random, halving_random and Optuna (1-1000)

branch_1_search_timeout.description: Branch 1 | Optional Optuna soft stop in positive seconds; null disables it. A running estimator fit is not interrupted

branch_1_search_random_state.description: Branch 1 | Seed for sampled parameter choices, separate from the heldout split seed and CV fold seed

branch_1_search_factor.description: Branch 1 | Successive halving keeps roughly one in this many candidates per round (integer 2 or more)

branch_1_search_resource.description: Branch 1 | Halving budget resource: training rows or estimator n_estimators. n_estimators requires explicit max_resources and a compatible model

branch_1_search_min_resources.description: Branch 1 | Halving starting budget: exhaust, smallest, or a positive integer

branch_1_search_estimator_min_resources.description: Branch 1 | Starting estimator budget for n_estimators halving (integer 2 or more; must not exceed max_resources)

branch_1_search_max_resources.description: Branch 1 | Maximum estimator resource count for n_estimators halving; enter a positive integer compatible with the selected model

branch_1_search_sampler.description: Branch 1 | Optuna sampler: TPE, random or CMA-ES; CMA-ES samples categorical axes randomly

branch_1_search_pruner.description: Branch 1 | Optuna trial pruner; Core checks whether the selected model and validation method support early stopping. none disables pruning

branch_1_search_pruning.description: Branch 1 | Allow Optuna pruning when model and validation settings support it

branch_1_search_tune_threshold.description: Branch 1 | Select a binary decision threshold from inner out-of-fold predictions. Requires probability output; final holdout stays untouched.

branch_2_name.description: Branch 2 | Unique branch name (portable identifier); also names its registered model

branch_2_task.description: Branch 2 | What will the model predict? regression = a number; classification = a category

branch_2_sample_weight_enabled.description: Use sample weights? false = No (default); true = Yes.

branch_2_weight_column.description: Training-only sample-weight column (excluded from model features).

branch_2_target_column.description: Branch 2 | Column containing the known answer during training, e.g. churn or claim_amount

branch_2_input_columns.description: Branch 2 | Columns the model learns from, e.g. income, age, balance. Separate names with commas; exclude record keys and the answer column

branch_2_preprocessing_recipe.description: Branch 2 | Named recipe from config/preprocessing.yml: default, none, example_imputer, example_frequency, example_imputer_frequency or example_all; adapt recipe columns to this branch

branch_2_pre_split_recipe.description: Branch 2 | Named recipe from config/pre_split.yml: default, none, example_complete_inputs or example_all; adapt recipe columns to this branch

branch_2_cv_enabled.description: Branch 2 | Use several training-only folds to score search candidates? No duplicate post-search CV report. With CV off, search uses a training-only validation split. Final test rows stay separate. Defaults: 5-fold K-fold, shuffle enabled, seed 42; the following questions select the fold policy before the data window. Model competition always enables the shared CV policy.

branch_2_cv_folds.description: Branch 2 | How many CV splits? 5 means five evaluations; more splits take longer (2-20)

branch_2_cv_type.description: Branch 2 | Fold method: k_fold, stratified_k_fold, time_series_split, shuffle_split, group_k_fold, stratified_group_k_fold, or nested_cv. Nested CV repeats an independent inner search in every outer training fold, then runs a separate final search Temporal CV automatically selects a chronological final holdout; its clock/window questions follow.

branch_2_cv_inner_folds.description: Branch 2 | Inner search folds for nested CV (2-20). Leave blank for the Core default. The strategy budget applies to every outer-fold search and the final search.

branch_2_cv_nested_type.description: Branch 2 | Policy at both nested levels; auto selects stratified classification or regression K-fold. Temporal requires a temporal final holdout and event_column.

branch_2_cv_group_column.description: Branch 2 | Group identity column, excluded from features. Final holdout isolates whole groups; disable holdout stratify.

branch_2_cv_gap.description: Branch 2 | Rows excluded before each temporal validation window at both nested levels.

branch_2_cv_test_size.description: Branch 2 | Temporal validation rows per fold; null uses the Core default.

branch_2_cv_max_train_size.description: Branch 2 | Temporal training rows; null expands, an integer creates a rolling window.

branch_2_cv_shuffle.description: Branch 2 | Shuffle rows for CV? Use false for time_series_split, true for shuffle_split

branch_2_cv_random_state.description: Branch 2 | Seed for repeatable CV splits. Keep 42 unless you want different splits

branch_2_split_strategy.description: Branch 2 | How to reserve test rows? random = random rows; temporal = newer rows for testing and older rows for training. Default source: full snapshot for random, rolling calendar for temporal. Override training_window_mode in an init file.

branch_2_test_size.description: Branch 2 | Share of rows reserved for final testing: 0.2 means 20% test and 80% training

branch_2_random_state.description: Branch 2 | Seed for repeatable random splitting. Keep 42 unless you want a different split

branch_2_stratify.description: Branch 2 | Keep similar proportions of each target class in training and test rows?

branch_2_training_window_mode.description: Branch 2 | Which source rows to use? full_snapshot = all; fixed_window = dates you enter; rolling_calendar = recent complete months; rolling_days = last N elapsed UTC days; auto = all for random, recent months for temporal

branch_2_lookback_days.description: Branch 2 | Total elapsed 24-hour days before each run to read, including holdout; enter 1 to 36500

branch_2_holdout_days.description: Branch 2 | Final elapsed days reserved for temporal testing; enter 1 to lookback_days minus 1

branch_2_window_timezone.description: Branch 2 | Timezone defining calendar month boundaries, e.g. Europe/Copenhagen. This controls selected data, not when the job runs

branch_2_monthly_lookback_months.description: Branch 2 | Total complete past months to read, including the final holdout. Example: 4 months with a 2-month holdout leaves 2 months for training

branch_2_holdout_months.description: Branch 2 | How many final complete months to hold out for testing? Enter 1 to total lookback minus 1; example: 2

branch_2_event_column.description: Branch 2 | Column containing when each record was observed, e.g. observation_date; used to select older/newer data

branch_2_event_time_kind.description: Branch 2 | How is this column stored? timestamp = database timestamp representing an instant; local_timestamp = database date/time without timezone; date = day only; text = a string. Choose yourself; setup does not inspect the table

branch_2_event_text_kind.description: Branch 2 | What does the date text contain? offset_datetime = date/time with Z or +02:00; local_datetime = date/time without an offset; date = only a day, e.g. 2026-08-10

branch_2_event_time_format.description: Branch 2 | How should this date text be read? Example: 10/08/2026 14:30 -> %d/%m/%Y %H:%M; 2026-08-10 -> %Y-%m-%d; 2026-08-10T14:30:00+02:00 -> %Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z

branch_2_event_time_timezone.description: Branch 2 | Which location does this clock/date belong to? Enter e.g. Europe/Copenhagen or UTC

branch_2_event_date_only.description: Branch 2 | This column has a day but no time. May we treat it as the start of that day? midnight = yes, 00:00 in your chosen timezone; reject = stop if such a value is encountered

branch_2_start.description: Branch 2 | Earliest observation to include, e.g. 2026-06-01T00:00:00+02:00. Required for fixed_window; rolling_calendar calculates it for every run

branch_2_holdout_start.description: Branch 2 | Observations from this time onward are test rows, e.g. 2026-08-01T00:00:00+02:00. Older selected rows train the model; rolling runs calculate it

branch_2_cutoff.description: Branch 2 | Stop before this observation time, e.g. 2026-09-01T00:00:00+02:00. This is a data boundary, not the job date; rolling runs calculate it

branch_2_filter_unavailable_results.description: Branch 2 | Do answers become known later? true = exclude rows whose answer was not yet available at the chosen time; false = use supplied answers

branch_2_result_availability_lag_hours.description: Branch 2 | When result_cutoff is blank, subtract this many hours from run start. Enter 0 to 87600; example: 48 excludes results available in the last two days. An explicit result_cutoff overrides this lag for every run

branch_2_result_available_at_column.description: Branch 2 | Column recording when each answer became known, e.g. claim_confirmed_at. This is a column name, not a date you enter

branch_2_result_time_kind.description: Branch 2 | How is this column stored? timestamp = database timestamp representing an instant; local_timestamp = database date/time without timezone; date = day only; text = a string. Choose yourself; setup does not inspect the table

branch_2_result_text_kind.description: Branch 2 | What does the date text contain? offset_datetime = date/time with Z or +02:00; local_datetime = date/time without an offset; date = only a day, e.g. 2026-08-10

branch_2_result_time_format.description: Branch 2 | How should this date text be read? Example: 10/08/2026 14:30 -> %d/%m/%Y %H:%M; 2026-08-10 -> %Y-%m-%d; 2026-08-10T14:30:00+02:00 -> %Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z

branch_2_result_time_timezone.description: Branch 2 | Which location does this clock/date belong to? Enter e.g. Europe/Copenhagen or UTC

branch_2_result_date_only.description: Branch 2 | This column has a day but no time. May we treat it as the start of that day? midnight = yes, 00:00 in your chosen timezone; reject = stop if such a value is encountered

branch_2_result_cutoff.description: Branch 2 | Use answers known by this time, INCLUDING this instant, e.g. 2026-09-15T00:00:00+02:00. An explicit cutoff applies to every run; blank derives run start minus result_availability_lag_hours

branch_2_max_rows.description: Branch 2 | Maximum rows transferred into Python memory per read; exceeding this stops the run. This does not randomly sample rows

branch_2_max_input_mb.description: Branch 2 | Maximum input data size transferred into Python memory, in MiB (64 = 64 MiB). Model training can use more RAM

branch_2_training_sample_rows.description: Branch 2 | Optional sample: enter 10000 to select up to 10000 eligible rows BEFORE train/test splitting. null = no sampling. Prediction rows are never sampled

branch_2_training_sample_seed.description: Branch 2 | Seed for choosing the same sample from the same table snapshot. Keep 42 unless you want another sample

branch_2_regression_model.description: Branch 2 | Choose a regression model. It starts with its default settings; README explains how to change them

branch_2_regression_model_weighted.description: Branch 2 | Choose a regression model. It starts with its default settings; README explains how to change them

branch_2_classification_model.description: Branch 2 | Choose a classification model. It starts with its default settings; README explains how to change them

branch_2_classification_model_weighted.description: Branch 2 | Choose a classification model. It starts with its default settings; README explains how to change them

branch_2_model_params.description: Branch 2 | Optional JSON object of fixed model parameters. For voting/stacking, include base_estimators and any base_estimator_params or final_estimator to define the ensemble. Other models can set this in an init file or generated config

branch_2_search_strategy.description: Branch 2 | Choose grid, random, halving_grid, halving_random, or optional Optuna. Core supplies a model-appropriate default search space; grid strategies evaluate its full Cartesian product

branch_2_search_settings.description: Branch 2 | Use Core defaults for this strategy, or customize its controls below

branch_2_search_max_candidates.description: Branch 2 | Maximum full-grid combinations to admit (1-10000). Grid and halving_grid run every combination, so preflight rejects a larger space

branch_2_search_space.description: Optional init-file search override; otherwise Bundle writes Core-derived editable lists into this branch. Edit its generated search_space or clear it to {} for automatic resolution.

branch_2_regression_search_metric.description: Branch 2 | Objective for choosing regression parameters on training folds; separate from the heldout lifecycle metric

branch_2_classification_search_metric.description: Branch 2 | Objective for choosing classification parameters on training folds; separate from the heldout lifecycle metric

branch_2_search_n_trials.description: Branch 2 | Trials or initial sampled candidates for random, halving_random and Optuna (1-1000)

branch_2_search_timeout.description: Branch 2 | Optional Optuna soft stop in positive seconds; null disables it. A running estimator fit is not interrupted

branch_2_search_random_state.description: Branch 2 | Seed for sampled parameter choices, separate from the heldout split seed and CV fold seed

branch_2_search_factor.description: Branch 2 | Successive halving keeps roughly one in this many candidates per round (integer 2 or more)

branch_2_search_resource.description: Branch 2 | Halving budget resource: training rows or estimator n_estimators. n_estimators requires explicit max_resources and a compatible model

branch_2_search_min_resources.description: Branch 2 | Halving starting budget: exhaust, smallest, or a positive integer

branch_2_search_estimator_min_resources.description: Branch 2 | Starting estimator budget for n_estimators halving (integer 2 or more; must not exceed max_resources)

branch_2_search_max_resources.description: Branch 2 | Maximum estimator resource count for n_estimators halving; enter a positive integer compatible with the selected model

branch_2_search_sampler.description: Branch 2 | Optuna sampler: TPE, random or CMA-ES; CMA-ES samples categorical axes randomly

branch_2_search_pruner.description: Branch 2 | Optuna trial pruner; Core checks whether the selected model and validation method support early stopping. none disables pruning

branch_2_search_pruning.description: Branch 2 | Allow Optuna pruning when model and validation settings support it

branch_2_search_tune_threshold.description: Branch 2 | Select a binary decision threshold from inner out-of-fold predictions. Requires probability output; final holdout stays untouched.

branch_2_regression_metric.description: Branch 2 | Metric for comparing regression models on separate test data (heldout). Lower error is better; higher R2 or explained variance is better

branch_2_classification_metric.description: Branch 2 | Metric for comparing classification models on separate test data (heldout). Some metrics need probabilities or specific class counts

branch_2_min_improvement.description: Branch 2 | Minimum metric improvement required for manual or automatic promotion; ties never pass

branch_2_quality_threshold.description: Branch 2 | Absolute quality gate; numeric required for automatic promotion or manual first-champion approval. Choose for your metric and task.

branch_2_quality_gates.description: Branch 2 | Optional init-file JSON object of additional heldout metric thresholds, or null

branch_3_name.description: Branch 3 | Unique branch name (portable identifier); also names its registered model

branch_3_task.description: Branch 3 | What will the model predict? regression = a number; classification = a category

branch_3_sample_weight_enabled.description: Use sample weights? false = No (default); true = Yes.

branch_3_weight_column.description: Training-only sample-weight column (excluded from model features).

branch_3_target_column.description: Branch 3 | Column containing the known answer during training, e.g. churn or claim_amount

branch_3_input_columns.description: Branch 3 | Columns the model learns from, e.g. income, age, balance. Separate names with commas; exclude record keys and the answer column

branch_3_preprocessing_recipe.description: Branch 3 | Named recipe from config/preprocessing.yml: default, none, example_imputer, example_frequency, example_imputer_frequency or example_all; adapt recipe columns to this branch

branch_3_pre_split_recipe.description: Branch 3 | Named recipe from config/pre_split.yml: default, none, example_complete_inputs or example_all; adapt recipe columns to this branch

branch_3_cv_enabled.description: Branch 3 | Use several training-only folds to score search candidates? No duplicate post-search CV report. With CV off, search uses a training-only validation split. Final test rows stay separate. Defaults: 5-fold K-fold, shuffle enabled, seed 42; the following questions select the fold policy before the data window. Model competition always enables the shared CV policy.

branch_3_cv_folds.description: Branch 3 | How many CV splits? 5 means five evaluations; more splits take longer (2-20)

branch_3_cv_type.description: Branch 3 | Fold method: k_fold, stratified_k_fold, time_series_split, shuffle_split, group_k_fold, stratified_group_k_fold, or nested_cv. Nested CV repeats an independent inner search in every outer training fold, then runs a separate final search Temporal CV automatically selects a chronological final holdout; its clock/window questions follow.

branch_3_cv_inner_folds.description: Branch 3 | Inner search folds for nested CV (2-20). Leave blank for the Core default. The strategy budget applies to every outer-fold search and the final search.

branch_3_cv_nested_type.description: Branch 3 | Policy at both nested levels; auto selects stratified classification or regression K-fold. Temporal requires a temporal final holdout and event_column.

branch_3_cv_group_column.description: Branch 3 | Group identity column, excluded from features. Final holdout isolates whole groups; disable holdout stratify.

branch_3_cv_gap.description: Branch 3 | Rows excluded before each temporal validation window at both nested levels.

branch_3_cv_test_size.description: Branch 3 | Temporal validation rows per fold; null uses the Core default.

branch_3_cv_max_train_size.description: Branch 3 | Temporal training rows; null expands, an integer creates a rolling window.

branch_3_cv_shuffle.description: Branch 3 | Shuffle rows for CV? Use false for time_series_split, true for shuffle_split

branch_3_cv_random_state.description: Branch 3 | Seed for repeatable CV splits. Keep 42 unless you want different splits

branch_3_split_strategy.description: Branch 3 | How to reserve test rows? random = random rows; temporal = newer rows for testing and older rows for training. Default source: full snapshot for random, rolling calendar for temporal. Override training_window_mode in an init file.

branch_3_test_size.description: Branch 3 | Share of rows reserved for final testing: 0.2 means 20% test and 80% training

branch_3_random_state.description: Branch 3 | Seed for repeatable random splitting. Keep 42 unless you want a different split

branch_3_stratify.description: Branch 3 | Keep similar proportions of each target class in training and test rows?

branch_3_training_window_mode.description: Branch 3 | Which source rows to use? full_snapshot = all; fixed_window = dates you enter; rolling_calendar = recent complete months; rolling_days = last N elapsed UTC days; auto = all for random, recent months for temporal

branch_3_lookback_days.description: Branch 3 | Total elapsed 24-hour days before each run to read, including holdout; enter 1 to 36500

branch_3_holdout_days.description: Branch 3 | Final elapsed days reserved for temporal testing; enter 1 to lookback_days minus 1

branch_3_window_timezone.description: Branch 3 | Timezone defining calendar month boundaries, e.g. Europe/Copenhagen. This controls selected data, not when the job runs

branch_3_monthly_lookback_months.description: Branch 3 | Total complete past months to read, including the final holdout. Example: 4 months with a 2-month holdout leaves 2 months for training

branch_3_holdout_months.description: Branch 3 | How many final complete months to hold out for testing? Enter 1 to total lookback minus 1; example: 2

branch_3_event_column.description: Branch 3 | Column containing when each record was observed, e.g. observation_date; used to select older/newer data

branch_3_event_time_kind.description: Branch 3 | How is this column stored? timestamp = database timestamp representing an instant; local_timestamp = database date/time without timezone; date = day only; text = a string. Choose yourself; setup does not inspect the table

branch_3_event_text_kind.description: Branch 3 | What does the date text contain? offset_datetime = date/time with Z or +02:00; local_datetime = date/time without an offset; date = only a day, e.g. 2026-08-10

branch_3_event_time_format.description: Branch 3 | How should this date text be read? Example: 10/08/2026 14:30 -> %d/%m/%Y %H:%M; 2026-08-10 -> %Y-%m-%d; 2026-08-10T14:30:00+02:00 -> %Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z

branch_3_event_time_timezone.description: Branch 3 | Which location does this clock/date belong to? Enter e.g. Europe/Copenhagen or UTC

branch_3_event_date_only.description: Branch 3 | This column has a day but no time. May we treat it as the start of that day? midnight = yes, 00:00 in your chosen timezone; reject = stop if such a value is encountered

branch_3_start.description: Branch 3 | Earliest observation to include, e.g. 2026-06-01T00:00:00+02:00. Required for fixed_window; rolling_calendar calculates it for every run

branch_3_holdout_start.description: Branch 3 | Observations from this time onward are test rows, e.g. 2026-08-01T00:00:00+02:00. Older selected rows train the model; rolling runs calculate it

branch_3_cutoff.description: Branch 3 | Stop before this observation time, e.g. 2026-09-01T00:00:00+02:00. This is a data boundary, not the job date; rolling runs calculate it

branch_3_filter_unavailable_results.description: Branch 3 | Do answers become known later? true = exclude rows whose answer was not yet available at the chosen time; false = use supplied answers

branch_3_result_availability_lag_hours.description: Branch 3 | When result_cutoff is blank, subtract this many hours from run start. Enter 0 to 87600; example: 48 excludes results available in the last two days. An explicit result_cutoff overrides this lag for every run

branch_3_result_available_at_column.description: Branch 3 | Column recording when each answer became known, e.g. claim_confirmed_at. This is a column name, not a date you enter

branch_3_result_time_kind.description: Branch 3 | How is this column stored? timestamp = database timestamp representing an instant; local_timestamp = database date/time without timezone; date = day only; text = a string. Choose yourself; setup does not inspect the table

branch_3_result_text_kind.description: Branch 3 | What does the date text contain? offset_datetime = date/time with Z or +02:00; local_datetime = date/time without an offset; date = only a day, e.g. 2026-08-10

branch_3_result_time_format.description: Branch 3 | How should this date text be read? Example: 10/08/2026 14:30 -> %d/%m/%Y %H:%M; 2026-08-10 -> %Y-%m-%d; 2026-08-10T14:30:00+02:00 -> %Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z

branch_3_result_time_timezone.description: Branch 3 | Which location does this clock/date belong to? Enter e.g. Europe/Copenhagen or UTC

branch_3_result_date_only.description: Branch 3 | This column has a day but no time. May we treat it as the start of that day? midnight = yes, 00:00 in your chosen timezone; reject = stop if such a value is encountered

branch_3_result_cutoff.description: Branch 3 | Use answers known by this time, INCLUDING this instant, e.g. 2026-09-15T00:00:00+02:00. An explicit cutoff applies to every run; blank derives run start minus result_availability_lag_hours

branch_3_max_rows.description: Branch 3 | Maximum rows transferred into Python memory per read; exceeding this stops the run. This does not randomly sample rows

branch_3_max_input_mb.description: Branch 3 | Maximum input data size transferred into Python memory, in MiB (64 = 64 MiB). Model training can use more RAM

branch_3_training_sample_rows.description: Branch 3 | Optional sample: enter 10000 to select up to 10000 eligible rows BEFORE train/test splitting. null = no sampling. Prediction rows are never sampled

branch_3_training_sample_seed.description: Branch 3 | Seed for choosing the same sample from the same table snapshot. Keep 42 unless you want another sample

branch_3_regression_model.description: Branch 3 | Choose a regression model. It starts with its default settings; README explains how to change them

branch_3_regression_model_weighted.description: Branch 3 | Choose a regression model. It starts with its default settings; README explains how to change them

branch_3_classification_model.description: Branch 3 | Choose a classification model. It starts with its default settings; README explains how to change them

branch_3_classification_model_weighted.description: Branch 3 | Choose a classification model. It starts with its default settings; README explains how to change them

branch_3_model_params.description: Branch 3 | Optional JSON object of fixed model parameters. For voting/stacking, include base_estimators and any base_estimator_params or final_estimator to define the ensemble. Other models can set this in an init file or generated config

branch_3_search_strategy.description: Branch 3 | Choose grid, random, halving_grid, halving_random, or optional Optuna. Core supplies a model-appropriate default search space; grid strategies evaluate its full Cartesian product

branch_3_search_settings.description: Branch 3 | Use Core defaults for this strategy, or customize its controls below

branch_3_search_max_candidates.description: Branch 3 | Maximum full-grid combinations to admit (1-10000). Grid and halving_grid run every combination, so preflight rejects a larger space

branch_3_search_space.description: Optional init-file search override; otherwise Bundle writes Core-derived editable lists into this branch. Edit its generated search_space or clear it to {} for automatic resolution.

branch_3_regression_search_metric.description: Branch 3 | Objective for choosing regression parameters on training folds; separate from the heldout lifecycle metric

branch_3_classification_search_metric.description: Branch 3 | Objective for choosing classification parameters on training folds; separate from the heldout lifecycle metric

branch_3_search_n_trials.description: Branch 3 | Trials or initial sampled candidates for random, halving_random and Optuna (1-1000)

branch_3_search_timeout.description: Branch 3 | Optional Optuna soft stop in positive seconds; null disables it. A running estimator fit is not interrupted

branch_3_search_random_state.description: Branch 3 | Seed for sampled parameter choices, separate from the heldout split seed and CV fold seed

branch_3_search_factor.description: Branch 3 | Successive halving keeps roughly one in this many candidates per round (integer 2 or more)

branch_3_search_resource.description: Branch 3 | Halving budget resource: training rows or estimator n_estimators. n_estimators requires explicit max_resources and a compatible model

branch_3_search_min_resources.description: Branch 3 | Halving starting budget: exhaust, smallest, or a positive integer

branch_3_search_estimator_min_resources.description: Branch 3 | Starting estimator budget for n_estimators halving (integer 2 or more; must not exceed max_resources)

branch_3_search_max_resources.description: Branch 3 | Maximum estimator resource count for n_estimators halving; enter a positive integer compatible with the selected model

branch_3_search_sampler.description: Branch 3 | Optuna sampler: TPE, random or CMA-ES; CMA-ES samples categorical axes randomly

branch_3_search_pruner.description: Branch 3 | Optuna trial pruner; Core checks whether the selected model and validation method support early stopping. none disables pruning

branch_3_search_pruning.description: Branch 3 | Allow Optuna pruning when model and validation settings support it

branch_3_search_tune_threshold.description: Branch 3 | Select a binary decision threshold from inner out-of-fold predictions. Requires probability output; final holdout stays untouched.

branch_3_regression_metric.description: Branch 3 | Metric for comparing regression models on separate test data (heldout). Lower error is better; higher R2 or explained variance is better

branch_3_classification_metric.description: Branch 3 | Metric for comparing classification models on separate test data (heldout). Some metrics need probabilities or specific class counts

branch_3_min_improvement.description: Branch 3 | Minimum metric improvement required for manual or automatic promotion; ties never pass

branch_3_quality_threshold.description: Branch 3 | Absolute quality gate; numeric required for automatic promotion or manual first-champion approval. Choose for your metric and task.

branch_3_quality_gates.description: Branch 3 | Optional init-file JSON object of additional heldout metric thresholds, or null

branch_4_name.description: Branch 4 | Unique branch name (portable identifier); also names its registered model

branch_4_task.description: Branch 4 | What will the model predict? regression = a number; classification = a category

branch_4_sample_weight_enabled.description: Use sample weights? false = No (default); true = Yes.

branch_4_weight_column.description: Training-only sample-weight column (excluded from model features).

branch_4_target_column.description: Branch 4 | Column containing the known answer during training, e.g. churn or claim_amount

branch_4_input_columns.description: Branch 4 | Columns the model learns from, e.g. income, age, balance. Separate names with commas; exclude record keys and the answer column

branch_4_preprocessing_recipe.description: Branch 4 | Named recipe from config/preprocessing.yml: default, none, example_imputer, example_frequency, example_imputer_frequency or example_all; adapt recipe columns to this branch

branch_4_pre_split_recipe.description: Branch 4 | Named recipe from config/pre_split.yml: default, none, example_complete_inputs or example_all; adapt recipe columns to this branch

branch_4_cv_enabled.description: Branch 4 | Use several training-only folds to score search candidates? No duplicate post-search CV report. With CV off, search uses a training-only validation split. Final test rows stay separate. Defaults: 5-fold K-fold, shuffle enabled, seed 42; the following questions select the fold policy before the data window. Model competition always enables the shared CV policy.

branch_4_cv_folds.description: Branch 4 | How many CV splits? 5 means five evaluations; more splits take longer (2-20)

branch_4_cv_type.description: Branch 4 | Fold method: k_fold, stratified_k_fold, time_series_split, shuffle_split, group_k_fold, stratified_group_k_fold, or nested_cv. Nested CV repeats an independent inner search in every outer training fold, then runs a separate final search Temporal CV automatically selects a chronological final holdout; its clock/window questions follow.

branch_4_cv_inner_folds.description: Branch 4 | Inner search folds for nested CV (2-20). Leave blank for the Core default. The strategy budget applies to every outer-fold search and the final search.

branch_4_cv_nested_type.description: Branch 4 | Policy at both nested levels; auto selects stratified classification or regression K-fold. Temporal requires a temporal final holdout and event_column.

branch_4_cv_group_column.description: Branch 4 | Group identity column, excluded from features. Final holdout isolates whole groups; disable holdout stratify.

branch_4_cv_gap.description: Branch 4 | Rows excluded before each temporal validation window at both nested levels.

branch_4_cv_test_size.description: Branch 4 | Temporal validation rows per fold; null uses the Core default.

branch_4_cv_max_train_size.description: Branch 4 | Temporal training rows; null expands, an integer creates a rolling window.

branch_4_cv_shuffle.description: Branch 4 | Shuffle rows for CV? Use false for time_series_split, true for shuffle_split

branch_4_cv_random_state.description: Branch 4 | Seed for repeatable CV splits. Keep 42 unless you want different splits

branch_4_split_strategy.description: Branch 4 | How to reserve test rows? random = random rows; temporal = newer rows for testing and older rows for training. Default source: full snapshot for random, rolling calendar for temporal. Override training_window_mode in an init file.

branch_4_test_size.description: Branch 4 | Share of rows reserved for final testing: 0.2 means 20% test and 80% training

branch_4_random_state.description: Branch 4 | Seed for repeatable random splitting. Keep 42 unless you want a different split

branch_4_stratify.description: Branch 4 | Keep similar proportions of each target class in training and test rows?

branch_4_training_window_mode.description: Branch 4 | Which source rows to use? full_snapshot = all; fixed_window = dates you enter; rolling_calendar = recent complete months; rolling_days = last N elapsed UTC days; auto = all for random, recent months for temporal

branch_4_lookback_days.description: Branch 4 | Total elapsed 24-hour days before each run to read, including holdout; enter 1 to 36500

branch_4_holdout_days.description: Branch 4 | Final elapsed days reserved for temporal testing; enter 1 to lookback_days minus 1

branch_4_window_timezone.description: Branch 4 | Timezone defining calendar month boundaries, e.g. Europe/Copenhagen. This controls selected data, not when the job runs

branch_4_monthly_lookback_months.description: Branch 4 | Total complete past months to read, including the final holdout. Example: 4 months with a 2-month holdout leaves 2 months for training

branch_4_holdout_months.description: Branch 4 | How many final complete months to hold out for testing? Enter 1 to total lookback minus 1; example: 2

branch_4_event_column.description: Branch 4 | Column containing when each record was observed, e.g. observation_date; used to select older/newer data

branch_4_event_time_kind.description: Branch 4 | How is this column stored? timestamp = database timestamp representing an instant; local_timestamp = database date/time without timezone; date = day only; text = a string. Choose yourself; setup does not inspect the table

branch_4_event_text_kind.description: Branch 4 | What does the date text contain? offset_datetime = date/time with Z or +02:00; local_datetime = date/time without an offset; date = only a day, e.g. 2026-08-10

branch_4_event_time_format.description: Branch 4 | How should this date text be read? Example: 10/08/2026 14:30 -> %d/%m/%Y %H:%M; 2026-08-10 -> %Y-%m-%d; 2026-08-10T14:30:00+02:00 -> %Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z

branch_4_event_time_timezone.description: Branch 4 | Which location does this clock/date belong to? Enter e.g. Europe/Copenhagen or UTC

branch_4_event_date_only.description: Branch 4 | This column has a day but no time. May we treat it as the start of that day? midnight = yes, 00:00 in your chosen timezone; reject = stop if such a value is encountered

branch_4_start.description: Branch 4 | Earliest observation to include, e.g. 2026-06-01T00:00:00+02:00. Required for fixed_window; rolling_calendar calculates it for every run

branch_4_holdout_start.description: Branch 4 | Observations from this time onward are test rows, e.g. 2026-08-01T00:00:00+02:00. Older selected rows train the model; rolling runs calculate it

branch_4_cutoff.description: Branch 4 | Stop before this observation time, e.g. 2026-09-01T00:00:00+02:00. This is a data boundary, not the job date; rolling runs calculate it

branch_4_filter_unavailable_results.description: Branch 4 | Do answers become known later? true = exclude rows whose answer was not yet available at the chosen time; false = use supplied answers

branch_4_result_availability_lag_hours.description: Branch 4 | When result_cutoff is blank, subtract this many hours from run start. Enter 0 to 87600; example: 48 excludes results available in the last two days. An explicit result_cutoff overrides this lag for every run

branch_4_result_available_at_column.description: Branch 4 | Column recording when each answer became known, e.g. claim_confirmed_at. This is a column name, not a date you enter

branch_4_result_time_kind.description: Branch 4 | How is this column stored? timestamp = database timestamp representing an instant; local_timestamp = database date/time without timezone; date = day only; text = a string. Choose yourself; setup does not inspect the table

branch_4_result_text_kind.description: Branch 4 | What does the date text contain? offset_datetime = date/time with Z or +02:00; local_datetime = date/time without an offset; date = only a day, e.g. 2026-08-10

branch_4_result_time_format.description: Branch 4 | How should this date text be read? Example: 10/08/2026 14:30 -> %d/%m/%Y %H:%M; 2026-08-10 -> %Y-%m-%d; 2026-08-10T14:30:00+02:00 -> %Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z

branch_4_result_time_timezone.description: Branch 4 | Which location does this clock/date belong to? Enter e.g. Europe/Copenhagen or UTC

branch_4_result_date_only.description: Branch 4 | This column has a day but no time. May we treat it as the start of that day? midnight = yes, 00:00 in your chosen timezone; reject = stop if such a value is encountered

branch_4_result_cutoff.description: Branch 4 | Use answers known by this time, INCLUDING this instant, e.g. 2026-09-15T00:00:00+02:00. An explicit cutoff applies to every run; blank derives run start minus result_availability_lag_hours

branch_4_max_rows.description: Branch 4 | Maximum rows transferred into Python memory per read; exceeding this stops the run. This does not randomly sample rows

branch_4_max_input_mb.description: Branch 4 | Maximum input data size transferred into Python memory, in MiB (64 = 64 MiB). Model training can use more RAM

branch_4_training_sample_rows.description: Branch 4 | Optional sample: enter 10000 to select up to 10000 eligible rows BEFORE train/test splitting. null = no sampling. Prediction rows are never sampled

branch_4_training_sample_seed.description: Branch 4 | Seed for choosing the same sample from the same table snapshot. Keep 42 unless you want another sample

branch_4_regression_model.description: Branch 4 | Choose a regression model. It starts with its default settings; README explains how to change them

branch_4_regression_model_weighted.description: Branch 4 | Choose a regression model. It starts with its default settings; README explains how to change them

branch_4_classification_model.description: Branch 4 | Choose a classification model. It starts with its default settings; README explains how to change them

branch_4_classification_model_weighted.description: Branch 4 | Choose a classification model. It starts with its default settings; README explains how to change them

branch_4_model_params.description: Branch 4 | Optional JSON object of fixed model parameters. For voting/stacking, include base_estimators and any base_estimator_params or final_estimator to define the ensemble. Other models can set this in an init file or generated config

branch_4_search_strategy.description: Branch 4 | Choose grid, random, halving_grid, halving_random, or optional Optuna. Core supplies a model-appropriate default search space; grid strategies evaluate its full Cartesian product

branch_4_search_settings.description: Branch 4 | Use Core defaults for this strategy, or customize its controls below

branch_4_search_max_candidates.description: Branch 4 | Maximum full-grid combinations to admit (1-10000). Grid and halving_grid run every combination, so preflight rejects a larger space

branch_4_search_space.description: Optional init-file search override; otherwise Bundle writes Core-derived editable lists into this branch. Edit its generated search_space or clear it to {} for automatic resolution.

branch_4_regression_search_metric.description: Branch 4 | Objective for choosing regression parameters on training folds; separate from the heldout lifecycle metric

branch_4_classification_search_metric.description: Branch 4 | Objective for choosing classification parameters on training folds; separate from the heldout lifecycle metric

branch_4_search_n_trials.description: Branch 4 | Trials or initial sampled candidates for random, halving_random and Optuna (1-1000)

branch_4_search_timeout.description: Branch 4 | Optional Optuna soft stop in positive seconds; null disables it. A running estimator fit is not interrupted

branch_4_search_random_state.description: Branch 4 | Seed for sampled parameter choices, separate from the heldout split seed and CV fold seed

branch_4_search_factor.description: Branch 4 | Successive halving keeps roughly one in this many candidates per round (integer 2 or more)

branch_4_search_resource.description: Branch 4 | Halving budget resource: training rows or estimator n_estimators. n_estimators requires explicit max_resources and a compatible model

branch_4_search_min_resources.description: Branch 4 | Halving starting budget: exhaust, smallest, or a positive integer

branch_4_search_estimator_min_resources.description: Branch 4 | Starting estimator budget for n_estimators halving (integer 2 or more; must not exceed max_resources)

branch_4_search_max_resources.description: Branch 4 | Maximum estimator resource count for n_estimators halving; enter a positive integer compatible with the selected model

branch_4_search_sampler.description: Branch 4 | Optuna sampler: TPE, random or CMA-ES; CMA-ES samples categorical axes randomly

branch_4_search_pruner.description: Branch 4 | Optuna trial pruner; Core checks whether the selected model and validation method support early stopping. none disables pruning

branch_4_search_pruning.description: Branch 4 | Allow Optuna pruning when model and validation settings support it

branch_4_search_tune_threshold.description: Branch 4 | Select a binary decision threshold from inner out-of-fold predictions. Requires probability output; final holdout stays untouched.

branch_4_regression_metric.description: Branch 4 | Metric for comparing regression models on separate test data (heldout). Lower error is better; higher R2 or explained variance is better

branch_4_classification_metric.description: Branch 4 | Metric for comparing classification models on separate test data (heldout). Some metrics need probabilities or specific class counts

branch_4_min_improvement.description: Branch 4 | Minimum metric improvement required for manual or automatic promotion; ties never pass

branch_4_quality_threshold.description: Branch 4 | Absolute quality gate; numeric required for automatic promotion or manual first-champion approval. Choose for your metric and task.

branch_4_quality_gates.description: Branch 4 | Optional init-file JSON object of additional heldout metric thresholds, or null
